stem: An Aboriginal 3-year-old has had several episodes of otitis media, and his preschool educator is worried about delayed speech; what is the best follow-up priority?

options.text: Routine anticoagulation review before future vaccines
Delay any further review until there has been at least 2 weeks of ear discharge
Stop influenza vaccination because otitis media is usually vaccine-related
Prioritise renal screening as the main expected consequence of otitis media

explanation: Hearing and language assessment is the best answer because recurrent otitis media can affect hearing, speech, language acquisition, and learning, so developmental concerns should prompt active follow-up.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because anticoagulation review is not relevant to otitis media follow-up or the developmental concerns described.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because recurrent otitis media can impair hearing and in turn affect speech and language development, making this the most appropriate follow-up priority.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because delaying review would miss the opportunity to assess hearing and language impacts early.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because otitis media is not a reason to stop influenza vaccination, and the main follow-up issue here is developmental assessment.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because renal screening is not the key consequence of otitis media; the important concerns are hearing, speech, language, and learning.
